findings.summary: Date/time ARRAY oids are not in RAW_TEXT_OIDS, so array columns are still parsed into JS Date and shifted by the Node runtime timezone
findings.evidence: RAW_TEXT_OIDS only contains the scalar oids DATE (1082), TIMESTAMP (1114), TIMESTAMPTZ (1184). The array oids (_date 1182, _timestamp 1115, _timestamptz 1185) fall through to getDefaultParser, whose pg-types array parser converts each element with the same Date parser the comment says is wrong ('shifts by the Node runtime timezone'). toCell() then JSON.stringifies the Date[] into ISO strings, so a `TIMESTAMP[]` column renders shifted by the backend server's local offset — exactly the bug this change claims to fix, just for array columns. The new e2e type table covers no array types, so nothing catches it.

findings.summary: Identity parser is returned regardless of wire format; for binary results it would return a Buffer instead of a Date
findings.evidence: `datasourceTypeParser = (oid, format) => RAW_TEXT_OIDS.has(oid) ? (value: string) => value : getDefaultParser(oid, format)` ignores `format` in the raw-text branch. If a query ever runs with `binary: true` (or pg requests binary for these fields), the value handed to the parser is a Buffer, and the identity parser returns the raw Buffer, which toCell() then renders as `{"type":"Buffer",...}`. Not reachable on today's call path (no binary queries), but the guard is format-blind.

findings.summary: Duplicate leftover test: 'queries real tables with rows' now exists twice, both creating/truncating/dropping the same _test_products table
findings.evidence: The diff adds `it('queries real tables with rows', ...)` at line 114 while the original copy remains at line 309 (asserting `expect(tablesResult.rows).toEqual([{ table_name: '_test_products' }])`). Both create, TRUNCATE and DROP the shared table `_test_products`; they are ordering-coupled and would collide if the suite is ever run with more than one worker over this file. This looks like an unresolved merge/edit artifact rather than intent.

findings.summary: Exported toCell() converts null/undefined to the literal strings 'null'/'undefined'
findings.evidence: `toCell(null)` falls through to `String(val)` → 'null' (and 'undefined' for undefined). ReadOnlyStore.loadQueryResults guards with `if (val === null || val === undefined) continue;` before calling, but toCell is now a public export (packages/sheets/src/index.ts:197) and is already called unguarded in packages/backend/test/database.e2e-spec.ts:301 (`toCell(rows[0].val)`), so any future caller gets 'null' text in a cell rather than an empty cell. The nullish guard lives at the call site, not in the helper.

findings.summary: MONEY assertion is locale-dependent and will fail on a server with non-en_US lc_monetary
findings.evidence: `[b.MONEY, 'MONEY', "'$1,234.56'", '$1,234.56']` — Postgres formats the `money` output type using the server's `lc_monetary` setting (thousands separator, decimal separator and currency symbol all vary). Unlike the other rows in the table, this expectation is not determined by the SET TimeZone/DateStyle the service now issues, so the integration lane's result depends on the Postgres container's locale.

findings.summary: Buffer (bytea) values are rendered as the JSON serialization of the Buffer internals
findings.evidence: `typeof val === 'object' && val !== null` catches Node Buffers, so a bytea column becomes the cell text `{"type":"Buffer","data":[222,173,190,239]}` (asserted in database.e2e-spec.ts:219). That is the accidental JSON.stringify shape of a Buffer, not a meaningful cell value; hex (`\xdeadbeef`) or a truncated placeholder is what a user would expect.

findings.summary: No sheets-package unit test covers the new toCell() helper; its only coverage is the backend Postgres integration lane
findings.evidence: toCell is defined and exported in packages/sheets but has no vitest coverage there — its behaviour (Date→ISO, object→JSON, null→'null') is only exercised from packages/backend/test/database.e2e-spec.ts, which requires a live Postgres. If that lane is skipped (describeDb guards on DATABASE_URL), regressions in toCell go entirely undetected.

findings.summary: Duplicate test named 'queries real tables with rows' added; an identical-named, stricter copy already exists at line 309
findings.evidence: `it('queries real tables with rows', ...)` now appears twice in the same describe block (lines 114 and 309), both creating/truncating/dropping the same `_test_products` table. The new copy asserts via `toCell(...)` with all-string expectations; the pre-existing copy asserts the raw typed rows (`{ id: 1, name: 'Widget', price: '9.99' }`). Duplicate names make failures ambiguous and the two tests race on the same global table name/lifecycle (the second one recreates and drops the table the first also drops), which is fragile rather than added coverage.

findings.summary: New exported `toCell` in packages/sheets has no test in the sheets vitest suite; its Date→ISO branch is exercised nowhere
findings.evidence: `toCell` is new public API in packages/sheets (also re-exported from src/index.ts) and changes ReadOnlyStore rendering from `String(val)` (objects → '[object Object]') to JSON. findings.summary: Unit spec mocks out `createClient`, so nothing asserts the new `types: { getTypeParser: datasourceTypeParser }` client option is wired up
findings.evidence: Both executeQuery unit tests do `jest.spyOn(service, 'createClient').mockReturnValue(client)` (lines 120-122, 161-163), and the mock client ignores constructor options entirely, so the new `types` option added in datasource.service.ts:204 cannot be observed. The updated assertions only cover the three SET statements. The parser wiring is only verified in the DB-gated e2e; a unit assertion on the options object passed to `new Client(...)` (or a direct test of `datasourceTypeParser` for DATE/TIMESTAMP/TIMESTAMPTZ vs a fallthrough OID) is absent.
searchedFor: grep for getTypeParser/datasourceTypeParser in backend tests

findings.summary: SELECT-only guard is bypassable: the validator inspects a comment-stripped copy while executeQuery concatenates and runs the ORIGINAL query text, allowing arbitrary multi-statement SQL (DELETE/DROP/SET) on the connected datasource
findings.evidence: `validateSelectQuery` strips `--[^\n]*` (sql-validator.ts:29) before doing the first-token, forbidden-keyword and semicolon checks, but `DataSourceService.executeQuery` interpolates the raw `dto.query` into `SELECT * FROM (${dto.query}) AS _q LIMIT 10001` (datasource.service.ts:148) and sends it through pg's simple-query protocol (no parameter values ⇒ multiple statements are executed). Postgres does NOT treat `--` inside a string literal as a comment, so the two views of the query diverge. Attack: an authenticated workspace member POSTs to /datasources/:id/query with `SELECT 'x--' ) AS a; DROP TABLE users; --'`. The validator's regex matches the `--` inside the literal and truncates the string to `SELECT 'x` — first token SELECT ✓, no forbidden keyword ✓, one statement ✓ ⇒ valid. Postgres then executes `SELECT * FROM (SELECT 'x--' ) AS a`, then `DROP TABLE users`, then a trailing comment. The same trick hides INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/GRANT and `SET statement_timeout = 0`, defeating both the read-only intent and the timeout/row-limit controls that the diff extends. The diff does not introduce the validator, but it modifies exactly this execution path (adding SETs at lines 143-145) and the guard reads as covered while it is not.

findings.summary: TLS certificate verification is disabled for all datasource connections (`rejectUnauthorized: false`), so enabling SSL gives no MITM protection for the decrypted DB credentials
findings.evidence: createClient — the object literal the diff edits to add `types` at line 204 — sets `ssl: ds.sslEnabled ? { rejectUnauthorized: false } : false` (line 202). Any network attacker between the backend and the user's Postgres host can present a self-signed cert, terminate the TLS session, and capture the plaintext credentials produced by `decrypt(ds.password)` (line 201) plus every row of query data. Users who tick `sslEnabled` reasonably believe the channel is authenticated; it is only encrypted to whoever answers. No hostname/CA verification option is exposed anywhere in the DTO (datasource.dto.ts) to opt back in.

findings.summary: SSRF / internal network probing: user-supplied host+port are connected to unvalidated, and testConnection returns the raw connection error to the caller as an oracle
findings.evidence: createClient (lines 196-205) uses attacker-chosen `ds.host`/`ds.port` with no allow/deny-list (no RFC1918, link-local 169.254.169.254, or localhost filtering anywhere in datasource.dto.ts or the service). `testConnection` (line 121) returns `{ success:false, error: (error as Error).message }` straight to the HTTP client, and `executeQuery` rethrows `pgError.message` (line 169). Distinct messages for ECONNREFUSED vs. timeout vs. 'password authentication failed' vs. protocol mismatch let any authenticated user map internal hosts/ports from the backend's network position (cloud metadata endpoints, internal admin ports) at 10s per probe (connectionTimeoutMillis, line 203). Confidence medium because reachability depends on deployment topology, but nothing in code constrains the destination.

findings.summary: Raw Postgres error text is forwarded verbatim to API clients, leaking remote schema/host/internal details
findings.evidence: `throw new BadRequestException(pgError.message || 'Query execution failed')` (line 169) and the `error` field of testConnection (line 121) return unfiltered driver/server messages. Postgres errors routinely include table and column names, search_path, file paths, roles, and resolved host/IP in connection failures. Combined with the SSRF vector above this is the probing oracle; on its own it is schema disclosure to any workspace member.

findings.summary: create() and update() return the full DataSource row, including the stored encryption payload, while findOne/findAllByWorkspace deliberately mask it
findings.evidence: `create` (line 44) and `update` (line 95) return the Prisma record unmodified, so the controller responses at datasource.controller.ts:43/67 and :104 include `password` as the `iv:authTag:ciphertext` blob — the very field that findOne (line 77) and findAllByWorkspace (line 68) go out of their way to replace with '********'. The value is AES-256-GCM ciphertext so it is not directly usable, but handing out the ciphertext plus IV/tag to every client (and into logs/caches) is unnecessary sensitive-data exposure and an inconsistent masking policy that will hide a real leak if the encryption scheme ever changes.

findings.summary: New e2e test duplicates the pre-existing 'queries real tables with rows' test instead of updating it
findings.evidence: The diff adds `it('queries real tables with rows', ...)` at line 114, but an almost identical test with the same name, same `_test_products` table, same inserts and same cleanup already exists at line 309 (visible in the diff's trailing context and confirmed in the worktree). The old copy still asserts the pre-change shape (`expect(dataResult.rows).toEqual([{ id: 1, name: 'Widget', price: '9.99' }, ...])`, line 370) while the new copy asserts via `toCell`. This is copy-paste duplication rather than reuse/update: two same-named tests racing on one shared table name, and the intended behavioural update was applied to a clone instead of the canonical test.

findings.summary: Query-result contract change (session TimeZone/DateStyle + raw-text date type parsers) is not recorded in the canonical datasource design doc
findings.evidence: docs/design/sheets/datasource.md is the canonical subsystem doc; its 'Query Execution' section (lines 156-162) enumerates exactly the session/execution behaviour this diff changes (statement timeout, wrapping, limits, response shape) and 'Current Limitations' #9 (line 205) plus 'Medium-term: Column type awareness' (line 221) describe the value-typing behaviour being altered. The diff changes the wire contract for `/datasources/:id/query` (DATE/TIMESTAMP/TIMESTAMPTZ now returned as raw Postgres text normalised to UTC/ISO instead of JS `Date`), which is an observable API/data-shape change affecting every client (frontend grid, REST API, CLI), yet no design doc under docs/design/ is added or updated in the diff.

findings.summary: Normalisation is applied at the connection/session layer, changing the API contract for all consumers, when the reported symptom is a display concern handled in `toCell`
findings.evidence: `SET TimeZone = 'UTC'` / `SET DateStyle = 'ISO, MDY'` plus a global `types.getTypeParser` override change what the datasource REST endpoint returns for every client, not just the sheet grid. The same diff also adds `toCell` in packages/sheets/src/store/readonly.ts, which already owns value→cell stringification (including a `Date → toISOString()` branch that these parser overrides make dead for DATE/TIMESTAMP/TIMESTAMPTZ). Fixing timezone shifting in one layer would have been sufficient; doing it in both leaves two competing normalisation points.

findings.summary: `toCell` locks in raw JSON dumps of internal JS shapes as cell values (Buffer/interval/circle), which reads as an unintended product decision
findings.evidence: `toCell` JSON-stringifies any object, and the new e2e table asserts this as the expected user-visible cell content: BYTEA → `{"type":"Buffer","data":[222,173,190,239]}`, INTERVAL → `{"years":1,"months":2,"days":3}`, CIRCLE → `{"x":1,"y":2,"radius":3}` (packages/backend/test/database.e2e-spec.ts ~lines 220-260). Encoding node-pg internal object shapes into spreadsheet cells conflicts with the doc's stated behaviour that values are displayed as strings, and freezes it via assertions.

findings.summary: Exhaustive ~40-type OID/cell-value matrix test is scope well beyond the three-OID behaviour change
findings.evidence: The change only alters parsing for DATE, TIMESTAMP and TIMESTAMPTZ, but the diff adds a full pg built-in type matrix (with a long commented-out catalogue of unusable internal types) that DDL-creates and drops a table per type in the shared integration database. This pins the current pg-types default parsers for dozens of types unrelated to the fix, coupling the suite to an upstream library's formatting choices.

findings.summary: `toCell` is promoted to the public `@wafflebase/sheets` API surface only so a backend test can import it
findings.evidence: `toCell` is newly exported from packages/sheets/src/index.ts, and its only consumer outside `ReadOnlyStore` is packages/backend/test/database.e2e-spec.ts (line 8). Widening an engine package's public API for a test-only consumer in another package is a questionable placement; there is no shared `core` package in this repo (packages/README.md lists sheets/docs/slides/frontend/backend/cli/documentation), so if backend genuinely needs this serialisation it arguably belongs next to the datasource module.

findings.summary: Raw-text OID guard is bypassed for array/range date-time types, so the timezone-shift bug it fixes still occurs for `timestamp[]`, `date[]`, `timestamptz[]`, `tsrange`, `tstzrange`
findings.evidence: `RAW_TEXT_OIDS` only contains the scalar `DATE`/`TIMESTAMP`/`TIMESTAMPTZ` OIDs (packages/backend/src/datasource/datasource.service.ts:20-24). pg-types registers separate parsers for the array OIDs (1182 `_date`, 1115 `_timestamp`, 1185 `_timestamptz`) and for range OIDs (3908 `tsrange`, 3910 `tstzrange`); those still hit `getDefaultParser` and produce JS `Date` objects built from the Node runtime timezone. Those values then flow to `ReadOnlyStore.loadQueryResults` -> `toCell` (packages/sheets/src/store/readonly.ts:73), which JSON.stringifies them, re-introducing exactly the shifted/altered rendering the change set out to remove. The new e2e type matrix (packages/backend/test/database.e2e-spec.ts:203-260) deliberately covers only scalar types, so nothing catches it. Fix belongs on the new code (extend RAW_TEXT_OIDS or override by format).

findings.summary: Duplicate `it('queries real tables with rows')` left in place — the pre-existing copy was not replaced by the new one
findings.evidence: packages/backend/test/database.e2e-spec.ts:309 declares a second test with the identical name as the one added at line ~112, against the same `_test_products` table (create/truncate/drop). Both run (jest allows duplicate names), doubling runtime and asserting overlapping behaviour in two different styles (line 358/370 keep the old deep-equal on raw row objects; the new one asserts via `toCell`). Looks like the new block was inserted rather than replacing the old one.

findings.summary: Design doc for the datasource module still describes the old query-execution and cell-conversion contract
findings.evidence: docs/design/sheets/datasource.md:156-162 lists the per-query session setup as only 'Statement timeout: 30 seconds' and says nothing about the new `SET TimeZone = 'UTC'` / `SET DateStyle = 'ISO, MDY'` or the raw-text date parsing; :164-173 describes `loadQueryResults` without the new `toCell` conversion rules (Date -> ISO, object -> JSON) that are now part of the sheets public API (packages/sheets/src/index.ts:197). This is a nested design doc, so the top-level docs link checker does not cover it.

verdict.reason: Verified directly in the repo. datasource.service.ts:21-25 defines RAW_TEXT_OIDS with only the scalar oids types.builtins.DATE/TIMESTAMP/TIMESTAMPTZ; pg's `builtins` enum contains no array oids, so _date (1182), _timestamp (1115) and _timestamptz (1185) are absent. datasource.service.ts:34-37 sends any oid not in that set to getDefaultParser, i.e. pg-types' parseDateArray, which converts each element with the same parseDate the comment at lines 19-20 says shifts by the Node runtime timezone; that element parser is internal to pg-types and is not re-dispatched through the client's getTypeParser, so the scalar override cannot cover it. packages/sheets/src/store/readonly.ts:32-36 confirms toCell JSON.stringifies non-Date objects, and JSON.stringify on a Date[] emits UTC ISO via Date.toJSON, so a TIMESTAMP[] renders shifted by the backend host offset while scalar TIMESTAMP renders raw text. The path is reachable because executeQuery (datasource.service.ts:127-174) runs arbitrary user SELECTs gated only by statement-kind validation. The e2e type table at packages/backend/test/database.e2e-spec.ts:230-278 contains only scalar types, so nothing catches it. Real inconsistent-output logic bug in the correctness lane.

samples.summary: Existing assertions were weakened to `String(rows[0].n)`, which passes regardless of whether the new global type parser corrupts non-date types

The PR's whole point is changing value parsing, and it loosens the assertions that guard parsing.

verdict.reason: The quoted `String(...)` loosenings do exist (database.e2e-spec.ts:85, :111, :163), but the regression class the finding says they stop guarding is covered by strict assertions elsewhere in the same gated suite. database.e2e-spec.ts:370-374 asserts `toEqual([{ id: 1, name: 'Widget', price: '9.99' }, ...])`, where `id` is a SERIAL/int4 asserted as the NUMBER 1 — a text-parsed int4 ('1') fails there. authenticated-http.e2e-spec.ts:203 asserts `toEqual([{ n: 1 }])` for `SELECT 1::int4 AS n` through the real controller+service+pg path. A broken `getDefaultParser` fallback would also break the per-OID table at database.e2e-spec.ts:199-307, whose expectations for CIRCLE (:242), INTERVAL (:254) and BYTEA (:219) require non-identity default parsers, and whose DATE/TIMESTAMP/TIMESTAMPTZ rows (:250, :252, :253) pin the actual new behavior (toCell emits `val.toISOString()` for Date per packages/sheets/src/store/readonly.ts:32-36, so a Date would fail). Both spec files are gated by the same `describeDb` flag (test/helpers/integration-helpers.ts:10-12), so the strict guards execute exactly when the loosened ones do.
